issues.description: The template's tensor-network simulate_ghz_state function signature omits the 'shots' parameter described in the problem statement and used in the solution. The template defines def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int) but its docstring and body refer to a 'shots' parameter (and even assert on shots), and the problem statement and solution expect def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits, shots). This mismatch is a structural bug that will prevent students from following the specification or running the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template function signature to include the shots parameter to match the problem statement and solution: def simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int]:. Ensure the docstring, asserts, and body reference the shots parameter consistently (as in the solution).

issues.description: The tensor-network GHZ simulation function is documented and implemented with a (num_qubits, shots) signature in the problem statement and the solution, but the template defines simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits) with no shots parameter. This mismatch of the function interface (parameter presence/name) for the same conceptual operation creates confusion for students about the expected API and how to call/implement the function.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template function to simulate_ghz_state(num_qubits: int, shots: int) -> dict[str, int] (and update the docstring to mention the shots parameter). This ensures students implement and call the function with the expected parameters.
